text_fidelity_a:
Klipsch ProMedia 2.1 THX Certified Computer Speaker System (Black) EDIT: Four-and-a-half years later I still love these speakers. They continue to sound good and functions perfectly well. I was initially worried by some reviews that stated these speakers wouldn't last but, in my case at least, they have. They get nearly daily use, some days 10+ hours, so they have held up well to fairly constant use.

I picked these up from our mail room, set them up at my desk over my lunch break, have been playing them about 15 minutes and already love them entirely. At twice the cost of my previous desktop speakers these are more than worth it.

For a few years I had a pair of relatively good [recognizable name-brand] speakers at my desk. I liked them well enough but they had one major flaw, which many people with small desktop speakers will easily recognize: when you get the volume down low (so as to not distract from work, to take a phone call, prevent an upset with others in the office, etc.) they get very flat and aren't worth listening to at all; instruments, vox, everything level off and lose their distinctness. The Klipsch 2.1 speakers sound SO much better at these lower volumes than my old speakers that I regret the years I spent with the crappy ones on my desk.

Other observations:

The first thing I noticed with these was that I had to keep the bass really low! they have a little mark on the dial which corresponds the the base level for CD/DVD which is about 30% of a full dial turn. I left it just short of that when I was tuning it by ear and only turned it up when some flatter tracks came on which needed a little boost. When a hip-hop track comes on however I am inclined to dial the bass back down just a little (apparently everything above that 30% mark is meant for gaming).

Then next thing which impressed me was the depth. The distinctness of notes and tones, the separateness between the highs and mids, etc. which these are capable of (at a regular listening volume, not quiet) leaves them sounding like actual speakers, not what you might expect from a PC/desktop speaker but what you would expect from Klipsch, even in this smaller package.

I would recommend these for anyone wanting to improve the sound out of their PC. I would also say that for a dorm or small apartment scenario these would be a fair option. The footprint on the sub only needs about 12"x10" and the satellites easily flank my dual-display setup and would work equally well on a bookshelf, coffee table, on top of a dresser, etc.

Anyone in the market for small speakers and who wants to get good sound for very little money these are a great option. If you don't want to pay $200 but you're willing to shell out $100 on lesser-quality speakers, I would suggest not wasting the $100--I wish I hadn't; now I'm out $300 and only have one pair of good speakers!
text_fidelity_b: Klipsch ProMedia 2.1 THX Certified Computer Speaker System (Black)

ELECOM Relacon Handheld Trackball Mouse, Thumb Control, 2.4GHz Wireless, Ergonomic Design, 10-Button Function with Smooth Tracking, Windows11, MacOS (M-RT1DRBK) I've bought and currently use both variants of the Relacon mouse. I'm putting this review on the wireless version.

Overall, 5 stars for the wireless with dongle, 3 stars for the Bluetooth. Unfortunately the Bluetooth one is a bit choppy with tracking, causing the pointer to jump to a random place on the screen often enough to be annoying. The dongle one doesn't have this issue for me. Otherwise they're identical in function and feel.

As a dedicated thumb trackball user since the early 90s, I love it! It is much better quality than any other ambidextrous thumb trackball I've optimistically tried over the years when looking for an alternative to the standard right (or rare left) dedicated handed thumb trackball. I have never been able to get comfortable or quick with finger trackballs, no matter how much I have wanted to or worked at it. Same with the Thinkpad trackpoint.

It is a physical relief to have a mouse that I can use in a neutral wrist position without having my hand or arm stretched out. It is especially nice to be able to transfer and use the mouse with my left hand when I need to type or do something else with my right.

I haven't installed the software or tried to remap the buttons. I just plug in the dongle or pair with Bluetooth, and Windows recognizes it. Since my displays are 1080 or smaller, I keep the speed or acceleration or dpi setting at 1 blink. The button is below the power switch, so I do accidentally tap it occasionally, but it's quick and easy to cycle back to 1.

The stand is more stylish than functional, and even with practice the mouse will sometimes slide right off, but at least it's included. Most of the time, I just switch it off and set the mouse on its side.
text_fidelity_b: ELECOM Relacon Handheld Trackball Mouse, Thumb Control, 2.4GHz Wireless, Ergonomic Design, 10-Button Function with Smooth Tracking, Windows11, MacOS (M-RT1DRBK)

The RCA protector plugs into one three-prong outlet, with a plastic support pin that's intended to slot into the ground hole of a lower outlet. Unfortunately the wall outlet I plugged the RCA into had slightly off plugs, so the support pin immediately snapped off in the lower outlet's ground hole. It wasn't hard to winkle out, but the RCA is now a little wobbly (and I assume has voided its own warranty...)

I'm a little iffy about these things as 6-outlets running off just one (with one ground,) but that's no different than all the other similar multi-adaptor units out there. The swivel feature functions fine, all the outlets work, and it says it has surge protection. We'll see what we'll see there; I hope NOT to test that function!!!

text_fidelity_a:
LG Electronics 70UK6570 70-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2018 Model) I bought this set for 4k gaming (PS4 PRO) and 4k films. Anything else like voice integration with google assistant was just a bonus that adds to the overall purchases and very happy with it.

The 70/75 inch model the only major difference is screen panel type. 75 is direct lit and 70 is edge lit. Features pretty much the same.

Out of the box the image using home mode was basic due the fact that all 4k TVs are set to automatic light detection and shifts the image to 'energy saver' slightly dimming them. Just go into the menu settings, picture setting and shut energy saving mode off. This is how all major tvs are shipped inbox. Its not a defect item. After shutting that off, the image settings work like normal. Vivid, sports, cinema etc they also have a professional tv set up for light and dark room. In case you want to hire someone professionally.

HDR effect is simulated HDR on SD content. Also a separate setting for HDR called: HDMI DEEP COLOR in 'additional picture settings' same location. They also have an option for eye strain, if its set on, shut it off. Its used for people who have eye strain from bright sets. I would keep HDMI DEEP COLOR ON to test that your HDMI is working with the TV, it will automatically turn on when it detects a blue-ray disk player with HDR or gaming system using it. Leaving it on, lets you know if the HDMI is compatible with it. Even if you're not using something with HDR. If the HDMI cant pass the signal, it will default to black screen 'no image detected'. In that case shut it off, and get a new HDMI.

After shutting off power saving modes, the tv works perfectly. Vivid images, sharp, major detail and awesome color. Whites are super white, but wont bleed over each other. Reds are blood red and blacks are dark. Everything pops off the screen, keep in mind i'm coming from a 1rst gen 4k tv that lacked a full HDR panel (10 bit). Slow remote response and lacking features that this set has. THIS new set fixes all that.. The blue tooth remote is responsive, fast and almost no lag, feel snappy and responsive. You can also download the LG app and use it as a pointer (like a mouse pointer on a computer). Easiest way to input information like passwords, email etc vs dialing them in on the remote. It can also be used as a pointer to navigate menu settings on screen with click being enter command.

LG has an app store, but haven't had a chance to play around with it. They give out free screensavers images in 4k, fireplace, beach etc and some basic games. In the future, i'll download wallpapers since my gaming is done on the PS4. They also have free apps for TV viewing from online channels. The set comes pre installed with Hulu, Netflix (controller has Netflix button), YouTube, google pictures etc you can also download free online shows that stream for free. From what I read online, Netflix is tuned to the TV for best viewing.

The set also has an update feature for firmware (under about TV settings sections) and you can set it to auto update. Once registered with LG, can also be done from TV. It allows you to use Google Assistance with a few prompts for basic set up. To fully use LG AI thinQ voice built in, you have to get a magic remote (under $50 bucks) and will be buying one soon, since I use voice features a lot. From google assistant from your phone, you can do basics, volume up +5, shut living room TV off and a few other commands that go threw google assistant (phone or google home) . The magic remote uses more the voice feature and you dont have to say: okay google, tell LG to turn off living room TV" saves you a step and allows you to use it for suggestions and what you see in the demo videos. Remember that AI ThinQ is working with Google assistant for results. Not a gimped voice feature like first generation 4k TVs.

My games look phenomenal, brand new including 4k films. Everything seems to have gotten a new coat of paint. The HDR really makes a difference in films and games. These set use HDR10 and HLG (Hybrid log gamma). The only thing it does not do is Dolby Vision. Its a Dolby version of HDR basically. Which to me isn't a deal breaker since HDR10 is more supported in films, streams etc

TV also supports fast wireless connection (wireless AC).

I have nothing negative to say about the set. Had an HDMI/HDR error and that was due to my HDMI not being high speed aka 'premium HDMI'. If you run into a similar issue with PS4 PRO, XBOX X or Blu-ray player. Connect directly to set should fix the issue and see if its the HDMI. Sometimes, like in my case, its an older HDMI that I had going from my sound system out to the LG TV. The PS4 was high speed/premium but the 2nd connection to the TV wasn't, so the chain was broken. Supported 4k but lacked bandwidth with 4k+ HDR.

This set has all major functions
VA panel
Wide Color Gamut (WCG)
4K Ultra HD Resolution
4K Active HDR
Ultra Luminance

UPDATE: 9/10/2018

Installed a new HDMI high speed cable from sound system out to TV from receiver and it fixed the 'no signal' sign when HDR was turned on. Leave HDMI DEEP COLOR ON. (it will pop up the logo) to let you know its working and not a black screen. if you get a black screen somethings wrong with the HDMI. When HDR is working and pops up the logo, go to settings (gear icons in remote), pulls up quick menu and HDR will be highlighted, but say HDR+Standard imaging viewing etc (can be changed). If you're using vivid (my personal choice) when using HDR, set it to HDR+ Vivid. When you do this again, and the TV detects an HDR signal again, it will remember the last HDR+(picture setting) mode you used. (HDR on or OFF) each has thier own image settings.

Random info: if you have a sound system connected to the TV, when using built in TV set apps (You-tube/Hulu etc) you may have to set the receiver/sound system to TV on its remote to get audio coming from the sound system. If you use a Blu-ray players apps, or apps from a game system like PS4 Hulu etc just setting the normal connection input should push the sound like normal.

text_fidelity_a:
Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I'm a software developer who works in a cubicle world with the heating system droning on above the ceiling (we're on the top floor of an office building - the HVAC is on the roof). These headphones provide an oasis of silence! The noise cancellation *seems* to be a cut above the others I've tried (Beats Studio at Target and a Sony set at Costco) although it's not really fair to compare as I didn't try the Bose under the same condition as the others (i.e. in a noisy store).

How good is it? The droning AC noise is completely gone. Voices I can still hear - until I play music. Even at low/moderate playback volume, voices are barely audible. People have to pat me on the back if they want my attention.

Comfort is excellent. I wear them on-and-off all day without problems. I imagine people with big ears might be less comfortable.

Power: the headphones use a single AAA battery. Keeping in mind that I maybe play music for 2-3 hours every day, the battery seems to last 2-3 weeks. As others have noted, these headphones will not work (i.e. play music) without power.

My one nitpick (and the reason I can't give it 5 stars) is the god-awful chord. It's some cheap plasticky material that I continually have to unravel by dangling the headphones by the plug end and letting the headphones rotate. It's really quite pathetic to put such cheap cr$p on $300 headphones - shame on Bose for not correcting this. Is it really going to affect your profitability so much you can't do something like the $20 Apple headphones that come with every iPhone (they're more rubberized and don't seem to get raveled).

Update for iPhone/iPad/iPod users: with iOS 7, Apple introduced a new way to invoke Siri (Apple's voice assistant) - instead of holding down the home button (or center button on the headphones) until you hear the Siri confirmation sound and then asking Siri your question and then waiting for Siri to accept your input, with iOS 7, you can keep the button pressed until you're finished talking - and avoid the delay Siri normally waits to know you're done with talking. It's a very useful feature.....and, it doesn't work with the Bose inline chord button :-( Not really Bose's fault, I guess, but I thought it worth mentioning.
text_fidelity_b: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

If the over-ear part of the headphones were a little more moldable, I might be able to make them work for me; the extra ear gels themselves are helpful in getting a good fit into the ear canal, but that doesn't keep them from falling off of me. This is why I'm knocking of a star but, again, the problem is not with the headset but with my own anatomy!

With that caveat aside, I love them! For a gardener who wants to listen to something outside while working, the FM radio works just fine and the yellow rubbery cord keeps them around your neck even if you do knock them off. The U.S. Military-grade protection features (against dust, moisture, and shock) make these headphones stand out from the pack.

The Bluetooth pairing and sustained connection with these is better than any other Bluetooth device I've ever used, although I tend not to use Bluetooth unless I'm up and about in the house doing chores. I also don't make or get a lot of phone calls, so we don't even have a cellphone account and depend on the occasional VoIP to get the job done. Meaning I haven't tested the headset features at all.

But the sound is crisp and clear, without mud, more like monitoring headphones used in the music industry. I feel no pressure when wearing them (holding them to my head with my hands, of course, to keep them from falling off of my teensy ears), and I know they would be very comfortable for me in daily use. Maybe I can come up with something to rig them with so they don't fall off. Because I really do like them.

Super loud, and will stop or at least make it difficult for a door to be opened wide enough for an intruder to enter. I tested one out on my husband by placing it at the door he normally enters through. It stopped him, scared him and did just what I hoped it would do. He kind of got mad at me and hollered a few explicatives but it was worth it! We have one door that is on a raised threshold so I set the door stop alarm on a book and the door hits it squarely when opened just a little bitty bit. It's loud - ear piercing loud and that's good as it should scare the bejeebers out of a bad person. On doors that have windows through which the unwanted guest might peer through and see the doorstop, just by placing a light weight towel or papers over it disguises completely. They'll just think your a slob and leave newspapers on the floor.

My mom was thrilled with her doorstops. Anything to help parents stay safe is money well-spent.

Be aware of how all of your doors open since they won't do any good on doors that open to the outside. The 9 volt battery was a tad difficult to install but I'm not complaining. For my mom I had to write in big letters with a felt permanent marker ON and OFF so she could easily turn them off when not in use and not waste batteries or scare her by an accidental alarm. We'll be taking some of these with us on vacation. These are really great!

I've learned to pick them up by holding the sides of them lest I accidentally hit the metal plate on top and hear it's ear-breaking scream. I've taken at least one of these on overnight trips to put against the door in our hotel rooms. It makes me feel a lot safer knowing this thing will scream if someone tries to break in.

text_fidelity_a:
BAOFENG BF-F8HP (UV-5R 3rd Gen) 8-Watt Dual Band Two-Way Radio (136-174MHz VHF & 400-520MHz UHF) Includes Full Kit with Large Battery Received as a Christmas gift. As I am not a licensed ham yet I have not transmitted on the radio, so I can't speak about any transmission issues that others may have experienced. To date I have only used it to monitor ham radio bands to understand how hams communicate.

For an affordable introductory ham radio, Baofeng radios are a good choice. Some ham "purists" seem to have nothing good to say about them, but many hams are welcoming of new operators and understand that these radios have the potential to expand the hobby.

The radio comes with a decent book (when ordered from BAOFENG TECH). There are also quite a few resources and videos online to assist in usage.

I found programming of stations to be fairly simple although a bit time consuming. There isn't really that much to it. If you are going to program in multiple channels or set offsets for repeater use then a programming cable would be a good investment. The programming cable also allows you to name individual channels.

There are some potential issues that can occur with use of this radio.

1. This radio covers VHF and UHF ham bands but also conflicts with police bands, city maintenance, and private corporation radio frequencies. There is the potential to accidentally transmit on an unauthorized band.

2. While this radio will scan UHF/VHF police, fire and EMT bands most have shifted to a new system. Some agencies are on the older systems and some simulcast on UHF/VHF but in general if you are planning on using this as a police scanner you probably aren't going to hear much.

3. There is no way to lock out the transmit key, so it is easy to press it while handling the radio if not paying attention.

As a monitoring radio the battery seems to last forever. If you are planning on transmitting a lot then an extra battery or 12VDC adapter may be warranted.

So far I really don't have anything negative to say. Good introductory radio.
text_fidelity_b: BAOFENG BF-F8HP (UV-5R 3rd Gen) 8-Watt Dual Band Two-Way Radio (136-174MHz VHF & 400-520MHz UHF) Includes Full Kit with Large Battery

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Plus with built-in Hub 1st Generation – Black [please see update below original review]

I bought the original Echo when it was first available for pre-order and have loved it. No issues. The opposite is the case with Echo Plus.

Doesn't understand me half the time.
Intermittent success using the remote.
Tried multiple times setting up groups to play music simultaneously in different rooms using it with my 2 echo dots and original Echo. Echo Plus responds by doing nothing, or playing a random song or stations, and nothing on the other units in the group.

I really hate returning things, but unless there are fixes in updates between now and the end of the return period, that's what I'll be doing. Seriously disappointed. Oh, and I called Amazon "help" so-called, and I knew more about how it works than the person I wasted 15 minutes on the phone with. It was a surreal convo.
= = =
UPDATE: This morning I got a call from Anthony, from Amazon customer service. First, I was blown away that they would call me to address my issues with Echo Plus. Second, he was knowledgeable, and in no hurry. While it remains to be seen whether every issue with EP is fixed, the problem with Groups was.

It turns out that Alexa didn't like the name I gave my group, it was that simple. My original Echo is black, my EP is white, so I called the group "Black And White". Suggestion: When setting up your groups, go with one of the suggested generic names--bedroom, living room, etc. Echo calls them "Common Names". I called mine "Backyard", even though my backyard isn't involved.

Regarding Alexa often not understanding me on the EP, Anthony suggested that I try switching from British english to American english. I'm going to try that, although I have used British english on my original Echo with no issues.

So, I've upgraded my review to 4 stars, and when and if all issues are resolved I'll be coming back to make it 5. Amazon support definitely gets 5 stars. Even though my first call was a disaster, the way they followed up was remarkable, and that's the important thing. Seriously impressed. Thank you, Anthony!
text_fidelity_b: Echo Plus with built-in Hub 1st Generation – Black

text_fidelity_a:
Kensington Wired SlimBlade Trackball Mouse (K72327U), Black I lived and breathed full-sized Kensington trackball mice from about 1987 until my last one stopped functioning and I couldn't find them anymore...probably in the late '90s. Tried some others; all had small, lightweight balls that gave none of the feel and control of Kensinton's...Expert Mouse? Was that what it was called back then too? Because it was the same general design as the current Expert Mouse, but the body was computer-case white.

Anyway, I had several of those (the quality going downhill with each iteration, as I recall) and loved them, and since they disappeared (as far as I could tell), I adapted, first to trackpads, which I've never liked much, and then back to traditional mice which don't give nearly the control of a trackball. Now, at last, it seems Kensington has again begun to produce truly worthwhile trackball mice, and this is one. Oh, it's _so_ good to have one of these again.

I'm doing that thing I hate when other people do it and reviewing the product as soon as I've gotten it up and running, without any kind of experiential history behind my assessment. I'll come back and update this in the future if necessary. But so far: I'm happy, happy, happy to have a real, full-sized Kensington trackball mouse again, with a heavy, substantial ball. There are only two things about this device that I'm not crazy about: In my old Kensington mice, the ball rested on physical rollers and I could give the ball a good spin and it would keep spinning for a second before stopping; it spun much more freely in its cavity than this ball does (so far...maybe that's something that will break in?) [Update: yes, after about three days of use the ball rolls more smoothly and silently than the old one on rollers ever did]. And the other thing is the scrolling mechanism. It's weird. Despite the KensingtonWorks software trying to make us believe otherwise, the "scroll ring" itself actually has nothing to do with scrolling, nor with anything else - the "scroll ring" is not even a control, but just a static piece of chrome trim. What makes the mouse scroll is twisting the ball this way or that from the top, as if it were a knob. At first I thought the "scroll ring" wasn't working because I was trying to use it without touching the ball...which does nothing. And now that I've figured out how scrolling works (you rest your finger on the "scroll ring" and push and pull the side of the ball)...I'm not crazy about it. I'm getting used to it, but it's just a weird way to scroll (I can't for the life of me remember how I used to do it on the Expert Mouse decades ago). It does work though.

(Update on the scrolling: I'm also not crazy about the way the KensingtonWorks software handles the scrolling speed adjustment. When you make the base pointer movement speed faster, the pointer continues to move smoothly, but just faster. When you make the scrolling speed faster though, you lose all smoothness - the software makes the scrolling faster by breaking it into successively larger and more jarring jumps. At the slowest speed, it's pretty smooth; at the highest speeds it's no longer really scrolling, but simply jumping abruptly from one screenful (or page) to the next. Increasing the scrolling speed just increases the size of these jumps, but I find them jarring and annoying starting at the second or third lowest speed setting.)

I also had to figure out how to program one of the buttons as a click lock, since Kensington doesn't call it that anymore, but calls it "left drag", "right drag", and "middle drag" (and I have no idea what the difference is between those three - I just chose "left drag" and it's working fine).

So far, those are my only gripes, all minor. So happy to have one of these things again! =) (Did I mention that?)

Enjoy...
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Wired SlimBlade Trackball Mouse (K72327U), Black

I find it difficult to type accurately using this keyboard. The keys are higher than those on other keyboards used around here. For example, the keys on the Mac and Acer keyboards are only about 1/8 inch above the underlying keyboard surface. The keys on the Perrix are at least 1/4 inch or more higher than the underlying keyboard surface. This is likely the reason for the difficulty. My hands and fingers are just average size so the logical conclusion is that the height of the keys is the root of the problem.

Other than this one issue, the keyboard is well made, there weren't any dead keys on the unit and the cable is sufficiently long to reach the computer without moving components around.

Should you buy this keyboard? No, if you've got large hands of thick, short fingers. Yes, if you're looking for a cost-effective backup keyboard and can adjust to the higher keys.

(Old Model) Seagate 2TB NAS HDD SATA 6Gb/s 64MB Cache 3.5-Inch Internal Bare Drive (ST2000VN000) I've been a fan of Seagate for many years, since their drives are generally long-lasting and reliable, yet inexpensive compared to comparable items on the market. Over the years, I've never had a Seagate hard drive that I felt died too quickly or had any kind of unexpected problem.

So when I was given the opportunity to test this huge Seagate drive, I was thrilled. Obviously, it's a bare hard drive, so you'll need to know how to open up your computer and connect the drive. Once I did that, the drive was immediately recognized by Windows and the drivers installed automatically. In order to make the drive show up and start working in Windows 7, I had to right-click on computer, click manage, double-click storage, double-click disk management, partition it, give it a drive letter, and format it.

This drive is built to handle 24 hour a day use as storage device attached to a network. Because I am a home user, I am not using the full capability of this drive, but for my purposes, having a huge hard drive to store my collection of horticultural images in raw format, this drive is faster than my other (non-solid-state) drive and I'm not noticing any noise when the data is being accessed.

Overall, this is a huge amount of storage space for the price and would make a great drive for home user or small business user. While you'll probably want a superfast solid-state drive to run Windows and other primary programs, I use a regular drive like this for storage on my computer so that I don't need to buy a 3 TB solid-state drive (do they even make those?).
text_fidelity_b: (Old Model) Seagate 2TB NAS HDD SATA 6Gb/s 64MB Cache 3.5-Inch Internal Bare Drive (ST2000VN000)

SABRENT 13 Port High Speed USB 2.0 Hub with Power Adapter and 2 Control Switches (HB-U14P) This is the largest (in terms of capacity) hubs I’ve every come across. It provides 13 USB ports, but does so in a relatively compact way. 12 of the 13 ports are arranged in a row, so while the hub is long (about 8.75 inches) its only about 1.25 inches wide. Port #13 is located on the end of the strip. All ports are USB 2.0.

It has two switches to control power to the ports. Switch #1 controls ports 1 to 7; switch #2 controls the rest. The power switches are small, but are rocker style with a good feel and a positive click action. The active ports light up with a somewhat bright blue glow.

The cable to attach to your PC is fixed and rather short (8 inches). Although it’s a good, stout cable, I would have preferred that it had an input port so a longer cable could be used. As such, this is not something that would work on top of a desk that had a PC on the floor unless an extension was used (an extension is NOT included).

It does include a power supply, which is a mandatory feature for a strip with this many ports. The DC input port is next to the USB input cable.

Good build quality and a relatively compact footprint given the number of ports, but the lack of a detachable input cable drops my rating by a star.

text_fidelity_a: sympa Desk Lamp, Dimmable Table Lamp with 3 Color Temperatures, 10,000 Lux UV-Free Portable Sun Lamps, Timer & Memory Function, for Home, Office This is a nice light therapy lamp that is very simple to use. The only parts are the lamp itself and a power cord. Once the lamp is plugged in, it’s simply a matter of touching the power button to turn it on, then pressing and holding the brightness button to set the lamp to the desired brightness level. At the highest setting it is very bright, too bright for me if I’m close to the lamp, but nice if you’re lighting up a room. Provided you don’t unplug the lamp after turning it off, the lamp will remember your desired setting and return to that when it’s next turned on. I’ve used other light therapy lamps that have a timer function; this one does not. Others are more portable, being the size of a small tablet or a Kindle. This one is rounder and looks to me more like a room lamp. Depending on how you wish to use the lamp and what functions you’re looking for, this may be a very good fit provided you plan to keep it in one place rather than transport it and don’t need a timer.

I thought I was upgrading to more power, more space, etc., but while some things improved, I've paid for it with truly horrible battery life. When I'd had it for less than a year, I started losing the charge at an accelerated rate. I tried turning off the wi-fi when I wasn't using the tablet, and that did help a bit, but it seemed as if everything I did was a huge drain. Surf the web for half an hour and I've lost 20% of my charge. Play a couple of games, another 20% (and not graphics intensive games either!) Yeah I can keep the wi-fi off, and turn off the tablet and not lose much at all, but what's the point of having a tablet then?

I contacted Amazon, and was told I'd have to to a complete system reset. The only thing this really accomplished, apart from a short space in which the charge lasted a little bit longer, was that I automatically got back all the apps I'd deleted because I didn't like them. So that was time wasted removing them from my system.

Nope, not happy. This Fire is only a bit over a year old, and I can't rely on it for anything but at-home use because I never know how long the battery will last.

text_fidelity_a:
LG Cinema Screen 55LM8600 55-Inch Cinema 3D 1080p 240Hz Dual Core LED-LCD HDTV with Smart TV and Six Pairs of 3D Glasses (2012 Model) The picture is astounding. A few friends and I watched [[ASIN:B004K4N64E Tron: Legacy / Tron: The Original Classic (Five-Disc Combo: Blu-ray 3D / Blu-ray / DVD / Digital Copy)]] on this, and althought I love the movie, I couldn't pay attention to the movie the first time through. I was too busy staring in awe at the way the clouds in the distant background moved, or the beauty of the image. I was told passive 3D is an image quality drop from HD because it projects half the image to each eye, but I'm calling that theory out. This picture is glorious.

When it upscales images to 3D it can get a little odd. I watched Naruto on it, and some moments were astounding, and some were just odd, as Naruto's eyes seemed to deepen into layers. Overall, I like the upscale. It's an approximation of 3D, but it's a darn good approximation.

My boyfriend wears huge glasses and these fit over them perfectly. On a lark, I put them on over my largest sunglasses, and they still fit, so if you wear glasses, even very large glasses, and you have any concerns that they won't work well with these, stop worrying.

As to connectors, there is one input for composite in, but it comes with a three-into-one adapter for that. The same for component in. Those are the only cable that come with it, so you will need those. I suggest [[ASIN:B003L1ZYYW AmazonBasics High-Speed HDMI Cable (9.8 Feet/3.0 Meters) - Supports Ethernet, 3D, and Audio Return [Newest Standard]]] as they are reliable and implement 3D transmission well. There are four specifications for HDMI, 1.4 being the latest, and not every device or cable fully implements the specification. The signal will downgrade to the lowest component, and with a TV like this, you don't want that component to be your cable. The difference is substantial.

There are four HDMI ports, and it doesn't seem to like connecting to an HDMI switcher. If you have a lot of devices plugged in, and you often find yourself wondering which input the DVD player is using, you'll love this. First, if a device isn't actively sending a signal, it displays as greyed out, and moves to the back of the list. Second, you can name your inputs. You select them from a list (I would have likes to call one Playstation 2, but had to opt for "Game") but it helps a lot.

The remote is kind of like a Wii controller. You wave it around and it points at things on the screen you can select. Very cute. If you find it hard to use, back up a few steps. It's counterintuitive, but it works. The cursor slows down.

For streaming it has the standard YouTube, Netflix and Hulu among others. The only tiny downside is that it doesn't yet support Amazon on demand videos. Plug in a [[ASIN:B005CLPP84 Roku 2 XS 1080p Streaming Player]] and you're set for streaming entertainment. I am in the process of replacing my router. It's in such bad shape that my Pingtest results range from B- to C when connected wirelessly. Whatever caching the set top does, it can provide perfect clarity even in such adverse conditions. Good to know if your Internet can have "off moments".

The energy star note that came on the TV (the yellow tag required by law that you see on all appliances these days) claims that this TV will have an Estimated Yearly Energy Cost of $14 with a range for similar models (45" - 49" TVs) going from $18 to $51. This is "Based on 11 cents per kWh and 5 hours use per day."

I wish I could give this 50 stars. It's perfect.
text_fidelity_b: LG Cinema Screen 55LM8600 55-Inch Cinema 3D 1080p 240Hz Dual Core LED-LCD HDTV with Smart TV and Six Pairs of 3D Glasses (2012 Model)

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Basics SDHC Class 4 16GB Secure Digital Card the plus to this card is obvious--it has a large capacity.  The con is that it is a little slow in picture-taking.  Depending on what you're looking for, you may be happy or dissatisfied. I used it in a Kodak flip-style camcorder/still picture taker and I liked the fact that I didn't have to worry about filling up the card.  I recorded at 720 and it did fine in the recording and in the downloading of the video--I really didn't notice any speed issues.  Picture-taking was a different story; there was a noticeable lag in taking still photos. I wouldn't dismiss this card for that reason, however, unless a difference of a second or so will matter to you.  Most of my still picture taking on vacation is done with a larger point and shoot Canon IS, so the lag time with the little camera didn't matter much to me as I either used it mostly for video as mentioned or took stills of landscape or posed photos.  To be honest, I prefer not to use such a large capacity card for photos anyway as I have a fear of something going wrong with the card and losing hundreds of photos as opposed to a few videos.  So I'm happy to keep this in the little compact video camera and snap the occasional slow photo. I wouldn't put it in my Canon for the above reason and also because the photos I take with that I'd be more concerned about the sluggish picture-taking.  Be selective about how you use it, and I think you'll be more than satisfied
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics SDHC Class 4 16GB Secure Digital Card

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Smart Plug, for home automation, Works with Alexa - A Certified for Humans Device We bought this plug when it was on a deal for $5. Glad we only paid that for it because the plug finally stopped reconnecting to the internet this week. Previously if the power failed it would reconnect on it's own. Occasionally it would just drop from the internet at random and then I could easily connect it. Most of the time, however, it would work great! We use it for a light since most of our house works on light switches that are not conveniently placed near the doors, so we trip around at night over stuff to get to the actual lights to turn them on without the smart plugs. Well after a storm and a power surge this past week, the plug in our bedroom showed as disconnected in the app. I have tried multiple times over multiple days to reconnect it. Once it gets to the internet connection part of the pairing "Provisioning Failure" pops up and it won't connect at all. I contacted Amazon via chat to fix the issue (after troubleshooting myself) and they only suggested resetting the plug (which I had already done) and restarting our entire home system and each Amazon Smart Device (which we did after the power surge due to other devices not working). After an hour and a half, they basically said well its out of warranty so you need to buy a new one. They did offer a discount but the discount was to be issued as a refund after purchase and the amount to be paid was significantly more then what I originally paid. We have 2 other smart plugs of a different brand that are as old as this plug that have had absolutely no issues to date and cost about $5 each when we purchased them as well. Not to mention the Amazon Smart Plug is bulky and takes up so much more space then the smaller round off-brand ones. Due to the fact that this plug didn't last a long time and the actual price is so high to begin with I would not recommend this plug. Spend the money on an off-brand!
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Smart Plug, for home automation, Works with Alexa - A Certified for Humans Device

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130) After initial euphoria, I have to say that the ROI is marginal at best. Briefly, here is why:

Positive:
1. Excellent day and night picture quality
2. Simple configuration and UI.
3. Free storage up to limit.
4. Rugged construction
5. Integration with Smarthings and other IoT.
6. Easy setup. Ensure you buy the condoms and mounting brackets for outside.

Negative: (Relative to price point)
1. Battery life is marginal. If you never have motion in an area great. But, think about that front yard where you have people walking by or cars parked just on the edge of your property. With roughly 10-15 activation per day, the battery drains quickly. I feel I would be better off with a perm. powered device.
2. While it has a standard micro usb port similar to virtually any android smart phone. You still require the Arlo plug to charge. Not a deal breaker, but painful.
2. App load times/camera viewing is slow. I have a 100 mb Xfinity internet connection with Netgear Orbi Mesh setup within 15 ft of the front camera. Connection in my house is not the issue. I have a Samsung S7 device. Be prepared to wait upwards of 30 seconds before authentication, app loads AND THEN the camera activates to see who is at the front door. It needs to be faster.
3. The absolute worst aspect of the camera is that recording does not start fast enough. Roughly 30 seconds of an event (or more) go by before capture begins. This is not acceptable. I have tried playing with various settings but unable to resolve.

Overall, I regret purchasing now. I should have invested the time and installed a fixed camera setup.

12-Jul-17 - I have lowered the stars on this product because of the incredibly poor support provided for both this product and in particular the ORBI which I also have. The warranty on both products which are similarly priced make zero sense. Stay away from NETGEAR until they get their act together.

17-Aug-17 - Finally heard back from NETGEAR and received confirmation in their user forums that the original screw adapter on the VMA1000 mount for the solar panel is too big. (gee thanks..I knew that) I was sent new screws that now allow the solar cable to be plugged in along with the VMA1000 mount. Why these are not highlighted everywhere and why there is no update to the Amazon listing as a bulletin or something to look for when buying the solar panel, I don't know. Overall, I would say NETGEAR is completely lost on any form of cohesive support and sincerely hope my product continues to work as I do not want to ever have to call or email again..

June 2020
I am done with Arlo. The product is over-priced and unreliable. Here is why:
I added the doorbells 2 yes ago and 2 of 2 have been rma'd.
2 of the cameras have been rma'd.
1 of the 2 solar panels has apparently died as not properly charging. This after less than 2 years.
I only realized recently that some Einstein at Arlo decided to have the wifi channel operate on the exact channel my mesh is on. There are clearly issues.
The camera has good and bad days from an access perspective. Some days they come up in about 30 seconds. Some they don't load..
The delay of 5 seconds before motion activates recording is brutal. You can completely someone moving fast.
Arlo support has become poor after being fantastic initially.

This product will be going the way of my Orbi soon. I am done with Netgear ( or formerly Netgear) products...
text_fidelity_b: Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi [Previous Generation] I bought for my mother as a mother's day gift. I also bought a Vera Bradley cover and a $50 Amazon GC to go with it. My mom is not the gadget type. No matter how many times I explain how to change TV setting from the Playstation to the cable box, which for our TV is a one button push, she just cannot do it. So, getting a Kindle was a stretch, however, I wanted her to have the ability to travel without taking a lot of books with her because my mom is also that mom who over packs and has too much stuff, which inevitably means she loses something.

So, the Kindle only gets use when she travel, but she has figured it out somewhat. She can't quite figure out how to purchase books or how to change the settings, which she just gets me to do it for her, but it has gotten a lot of use because she does take it with her instead of a bunch of books. In my use of this Kindle, I find it somewhat clumsy, slow, and some of the icons are not self explanatory and takes a few tries going back and forth. What I do like is that the screen is the exact size of a paperback book, there is no glare whatsoever, which is a problem I have with my iPad, and the light in the screen is perfect for reading at night without a lamp on. The ability to have all of Amazon's e-books at your fingertips is nice if you have a Wi-Fi connection. I don't see a reason to get the 3G as this is just a Kindle for reading only, thus, I and my mother can wait til a Wi-Fi connection is available to download another book if need be. However, you can download multiple books at a time so if you just can't stand not having something to do for 20-30 mins, I would suggest downloading more than one.

Battery life is out of control! I have never seen this go below 50% even after hours of use. One downside is that the plug to charge it is not included so you will have to also pay for that as well. It is also very lightweight, and if you have a little case it's like holding an actual paperback, unlike an iPad which is much heavier and cumbersome to read e-books on.

However, overall, I'm old school. I like paper books. The smell, the ability to write notes and see those notes on the margins, the feel of the paper between my fingers. I can go my references quicker and don't have to worry about running out of memory space because my books stay on a shelf until I need them. So, I recommend this for travel only for the sake making room in your carryon. It is easy to use once you learn all the little quirks. Otherwise, the geek/nerd in me just always goes back to actual black and white.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi [Previous Generation]

It takes a while to get everything adjusted and level, so if you have a favorite position to use this table in you might just want to leave it in that position rather than go through all the adjustments necessary to change it each time. Once it's in position though the articulating joints are locked in place and the table is very stable. It definitely does what it claims to do and seems to be very sturdy, so I think it should last a long time. Very functional, well made & useful.

text_fidelity_a:
3DConnexion 3DX-700059 Spacemouse Compact 3D Mouse At first I was skeptical about the idea of using my left hand for this. I was initially expecting it to be a replacement mouse for my right hand, but after more research I understood what they are trying to do. I must say that it's much easier to use than I expected, and operating it with my left hand works just fine.

I was also hesitant because of the price. However, this mouse is fantastic. Worth every penny. I'm using it with SketchUp, and it's vastly easier and faster than the normal built-in navigation tools. It's hard to articulate just how awesome this is. Once you get used to it, it's instinctive and effortless, and moving around the model is so easy! You will absolutely love it.

There was one tricky thing during the setup, however. I plugged it in, loaded the driver, and launched SketchUp. Then I found and opened the configuration window to customize it for SketchUp. The info I had found showed that configuration window with "SketchUp" at the top, and the SketchUp-specific options. But my configuration window didn't have anything specific to SketchUp. It said Windows Explorer at the top instead of SketchUp. I thought I was missing a driver. I messed around a log time, and looked through lots of online info.

At one point, I noticed it said Chrome instead of Windows Explorer. That's when I figured it out. The configuration window changes by itself, based on what application is active. I had SketchUp running in the background, but my most recent activity was with Windows Explorer and then Chrome. With the configuration window open, I clicked over into the SketchUp window, and suddenly the configuration window said SketchUp at the top, and the the SketchUp-specific settings appeared. I wish that had been in the instructions somewhere!!

At first I didn't bother programming the buttons, but later I tried it, and that's an awesome feature. For Sketchup, I programmed one button to be "remove guides", and the other is "paste in place". Hitting those buttons is much faster than finding those things in the menu each time. However, I discovered that I need to make sure I'm not moving through the model when I press the "paste in place" button, or the mouse locks up, and I need to restart SketchUp. But as long as I make sure I'm not moving when I press it, I never have that problem anymore.

Anyway, you will absolutely love this. After using it, I no longer had any doubt about it being worth the money. It's worth every penny. I would give it 6 stars if I could.
text_fidelity_b: 3DConnexion 3DX-700059 Spacemouse Compact 3D Mouse

What I do like is that they fit my ear like a glove, and the sound quality is phenominal. It sounds like a much bigger driver. I am not an audiophile, but it really sounds great. Maybe it is the mid that come in fuller giving it a rich sound.

I have had some charging issues. Sometimes I find that only one of the headphones are dead and the other is fully charged. However, fit and sound are my most important details so these are my favorite. For the price I can purchase three and keep them in different places. If I lose one or have a charging issue I can replace it with the extra. This makes much more sense than keeping the aI do not more.

Edit: I changed from 3 to 5 stars. I have owned these now for almost one year, and use them probably every day. There has been no decrease in performance or battery life. I was so accustomed to my previous ear buds that I did not like these much at first. However, the sound is balanced, the battery life is great, and I really like the charging case. I have never actually times the batter life, but it is probably about 7-8 hours on a full charge. There are sooo many choices now for bluetooth ear buds, but these are a safe bet and most people should be happy. I am however not an audiophile, and someone who truly is may want to spend more on a Bose, or whatever the best ear buds are nowadays. My previous ones were more bass heavy, but these are better balanced. They do stay in the ear, unless I go to lay down on my back; I then have to push them back into my ear.

SUDOKEJI 1000W Pure Sine Wave Inverter Power Inverter Peak Power 2000W 12V DC to 110V 120V AC with LED Display 3 AC Outlets & USB Port for RV Truck Boat This worked just fine for powering a few small items. When choosing what you are going to run on this add up the total wattage of all devices, then add at least 50% more to account for peaks or spikes in the power draw. For example if your coffee maker draws 500 watts, your laptop 300 watts, and your toaster 200 watts (total, 1000 watts) you should account for the extra 50% (1000watts + 500 watts (the 50%)=1500watts). In this example, a minimum 1500 watt inverter should be used.

If the item is motor driven, it requires additional start-up (surge) wattage (typically 2-3 times the continuous wattage required) to start the device. For example, a miter saw that runs at 700 watts might require 1400 watts to start up. If your inverter only supplies 1000 watts, you will not be able to start it up. In this case, you would want to select an inverter rated at least 1400 surge watts to handle start-up needs.

I understand how wattage works and for someone who doesn't, any inverter could fail if overloaded with more power than it can handle. An overload feature that automatically shuts the device off would be helpful for anyone who is unsure. This has an overload feature, but if you blow a fuse, you'll have to replace it. Do your research and know how this works, and it'll work fine.
text_fidelity_b: SUDOKEJI 1000W Pure Sine Wave Inverter Power Inverter Peak Power 2000W 12V DC to 110V 120V AC with LED Display 3 AC Outlets & USB Port for RV Truck Boat

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 This will be a fairly detailed and honest review.

1. Who is this for?
This computer is what I would consider a gateway computer. Those who are looking at upgrading a fairly old or not so powerful laptop and are looking to do a little more productivity, this is a great option.

2. What do you get?
Well you can probably read the description, however it's worth noting. You get an Intel i7 7500u CPU (dual core with 4 threads) 12gb DDR4 RAM, Nvidia 940mx GPU, a 256gb SSD, 15.6" 1080p screen, fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard.

The reason I mention all of the feautures is because you would be hardpressed to find another laptop with these features for the same price. To my knowledge there is not laptop on the market for $800 with an i7, dedicated graphics, 12gb of RAM and an SSD. This is really one of the best values on the market right now.

With all of that said, this isn't for everyone. If you want to do extensive gaming, this is not for you. Can it game? Yes, light gaming can be achieved, however it isn't marketed as a gaming laptop. Is this for someone who wants to do editing (video, audio, photos)? Yes, again light editing can be achieved.

What blew me away with this computer is the speakers! They are fantastic! I usually use headphones and would consider myself somewhat picky with sound, and for laptop speakers these are really something great.

This computer is really a middle of the pack all arounders dream. If you dabble in a little of this and a little of that but don't do anything professionally or extremely serious, this is really all you need.

Also, everyone's experience is different. Some hate loud fans, and if this is pushed the fans will be audible. Some don't like that the backlit keyboard times out after 30 seconds of no use. These things really don't bother me.

Lastly, the versatility of this laptop is really great. I've bought tablets and sold them because I couldn't justify having a laptop and tablet, then bought tablets again because I missed the things I could do with them that I was missing on a laptop. This solved all of those issues except size. It's pretty big, which for some is a plus others its not.

Overall, if you are looking at upgrading and don't want to spend $1,200-2,000 on a flagship model laptop this is a great option! I can't recommend this enough.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I received a Kindle as a gift, and it has taken over my reading life. I'm sad when a book is only available in print and delighted when there is a Kindle version. It's not AS comfortable as a print book, it's MORE comfortable than a print book. The font is amazing. It's easy to use, and for people who knit, it sits nicely in a bookstand on or a reader's pillow to read while knitting.

I have the Sony eReader. I used to own the rocket. I see the Kindle as the real future of ebooks, and I really want ebooks to succeed for a few reasons.

One is storage. If you are a bibliophile, you probably have a book army ready to take over your home. We avid readers are forced to cull our libraries to make room for new books. No more. I would suggest opening a free account with a service like Goodreads to categorize books, since with the Kindle you can't set up a "history" section and a "fantasy" section, but that's so minor. I never could keep those organized in my print library as well, and many books fall into multiple categories anyway. Do I need to mention that ebooks don't yellow and decay over time?

Two is portability. If you are the type to carry many books at once (I am--some for study and some for pleasure reading along with a newspaper) then this is the easiest way to do it.

Three is the glorious possibility that books will never go "out of print" again, because there is no "print" overhead, just a little meg sitting in a several terrabyte raid array somewhere. Books will always be a minute away.

Four is the idea that books will be instantly large print and still small, and easy to tote around. My eyes are still quite good, but I'd love to think, when age degrades them someday, I'll still be able to read the latest releases easily.

Five is the instant availability of hot books. When Brisingr came out, it was sitting on my Kindle that morning. Compare that to the sometimes day-long wait we went through for the Harry Potter books (and books that size are yet another reason ebooks rock). I love having the New York Times delivered, but can't stand it when the delivery boy loses the key and rings my bell at 4 in the morning. This is the best of both worlds.

Six is the ease of reading large online documents, such as those from Gutenberg or a friend's novel (and don't we all have someone who sends us large files to read from time to time?)

Seven is the price of the books. Everything is cheaper on the Kindle and some books are frighteningly inexpensive. I bought the Talmud for 99 cents. A collection of the first five books in the John Carter on Mars series for 99 cents. And the entire collection of the Wizard of Oz books for, you guessed it, 99 cents.

Other e-readers hit close to the mark; the Kindle got it right. I only want two things. I want color and I want Amazon to hit that goal of having every book (including comics and manga please) available for the Kindle. Overall, the day of the ebook truly arrived with the Kindle and I couldn't be happier.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) When my husband recently purchased a [[ASIN:B0071N6AC6 netbook]], he wasn't using his Kindle Fire nearly as much, and I inherited it. I had recently dumped my cable TV service in favor of using the Fire to watch online the few news and TV dramas that I normally had used my TiVo to record. I found that my Internet connection through a wifi router has a really hard time playing videos via the Fire. It would often lose connectivity or freeze up when my iPhone was working fine using the same connection, playing the same shows.

The Fire has a gorgeous interface, though, for reading eBooks compared to my Kindle Keyboard. However, I've been using a Kindle app so frequently the past few months on my iPhone, that both the Kindle Keyboard and the Kindle Fire feel too cumbersome to bother with most of the time in comparison as an eReader.

For searching the Internet, the Fire has an easier interface than the iPhone, so I use it more often for that, unless I don't have it with me--I always have my iPhone with me.

I don't use the Fire for MP3. It is just too huge compared to my tiny MP3 player.

I don't have magazine subscriptions in electronic form, so I don't use it for that, though I know I could if I wanted to.

I understand the Fire can support PDF, but I haven't used it for that yet.

seenda Ergonomic Mouse, Wireless Vertical Mouse - Rechargeable Optical Mice for Multi-Purpose (Bluetooth 5.0 + Bluetooth 3.0 + USB Connection) Compatible Apple Mac and Windows Computers - Black This being the first time I have used an ergonomic mouse I had certain expectations regarding how it would solve the problem I usually have with mice. While it removes the pressure points from the center of the wrist the tilt move that point to the bone on the side of your wrist. This is easily cured by a cushioned mouse pad. So why then use it if you still need a soft spot for your wrist? Ease of use! The mouse has a variable sensitivity rate that is nice and high for us power users (move the mouse a fraction and you can span the entire screen), or dial back the sensitivity for doing very fine and slow cursor movements. The two buttons on the side are excellent as the back and forward buttons. I have become an active user of the back button. Saves having to move the mouse to the screen icon to go back.
The Bluetooth connection works about 90% of the time. When you walk away for a bit, or don't move the mouse for a while it goes to sleep. Which requires you to hit a button to make it wake back up. On my Linux environment that translates to a few seconds of time wasted on movements and button play to get Linux to realize the mouse is in play. Using the USB adapter for 2.5Gz communications, there is no waiting for anything to wake up. It simply works. Downside: it eats another port on your computer. If you have limited ports but also have Bluetooth, your best bet is to keep it on Bluetooth.
Overall I have enjoyed its speed and button options. Work very well for what I do. Takes a little getting used to but you'll be a pro in a short amount of time.
text_fidelity_b: seenda Ergonomic Mouse, Wireless Vertical Mouse - Rechargeable Optical Mice for Multi-Purpose (Bluetooth 5.0 + Bluetooth 3.0 + USB Connection) Compatible Apple Mac and Windows Computers - Black

Sony Walkman NWZA17SLV 64 GB Hi-Res Digital Music Player (Silver) I am writing this review because after reading the few reviews available it sounded like this would be a great Media Player. But after receiving the player (a Christmas gift from my wife) I have to wonder if most of the people who reviewed the unit have actually used or even seen one in person. So I reread the reviews and noticed a trend that they don't actually say anything about using the player (all except one).
So here is a real user review.
The good. (I use it for music playback only)
The sound on the player is superb. I rip my cd's using the FLAC format and I have listed to playback using Wired (Grado's) and Bluetooth headphones. I have also listened to it on my home stereo using wired and a Bluetooth connection. There is a slight difference in the tonal quality but in a noisy environment my ears can't tell the difference. Sony digital processor does seem to color the music a little but it is on the warm side so it not objectionable.
I must say I love the sound of this player.
The media program (Media Go) that comes with it is very good for ripping music in any format that the player supports. Setting up playlist to send to the player is a breeze. The program does not have the options of JRiver Media Center but it is simpler to use.
The Bad
It is cheaply built - If feels like a toy. I do not believe it will stand up to daily use. Not a quality product that I have come to expect from Sony. For the price of this unit I expect it to at least have the build quality of my FiiO player or my cassette Walkman (which still works)
Bluetooth- It's a joke. My main reason of wanting this player was Bluetooth connectivity. If you disconnect it from the headphones, stereo -car and home, It take at least three tries for it to reconnect the next time you want to use it and you have to navigate to the Bluetooth screen to do it.
This creates a problem on its own. If you were listening to your playlist and stop at a particular track you now loose that place unless you navigate back to the home screen (more on that later) and bookmark your spot before you try and reconnect to your Bluetooth playback source. This is a major pain.
Screen Navigation. The player has 4 main buttons. The toggle button which surrounds the play and pause button is use for navigation. The navigation is more cumbersome -not user friendly- than it needs to be. Try and navigate while you are working out or somewhere not so well lit and it is frustrating at best. At this price it should have a touch screen. My 29 dollar SanDisk player is easier to use that this setup.
The next problem. You really can't power down the player. Once you power down the player if you accidently touch any button on the player it powers back up. I keep the player in a soft case clipped to my belt. I have bumped the player while in the case and have ended up with a dead battery the next time I wanted to use it.
There are other problems but they are minor and I can live with those.
If Sony wants to play in this market (no pun intended) these major flaws need to be fixed.
Tried to post a review on Sony's web site and they would not let it post. So I don't trust any reviews on their web site at this point. This is why I am posting it here to at least let potential buyers be aware of what it is really like to use this player.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Walkman NWZA17SLV 64 GB Hi-Res Digital Music Player (Silver)

Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) The Fire and I have been inseparable since its arrival. I love this tablet! The professional reviews I'd read before I received it set my expectations pretty low by saying it's a nice device for the price, but the reality is that it's just a really nice device!

I have an iPad (first generation..., so no camera), and I like it, but I'm not a power iPad user. I use it to stream movies, read, surf the internet, and play games. The Kindle Fire does all of those things, but has the added bonus of being more portable, which is a pretty big deal to me. My iPad has always been a home device for me because it's too big to realistically throw in my purse. The Fire is the perfect size for portability! However, it is still significantly larger than a smartphone, so I can read or watch movies without squinting or holding a device up to my face.

One big weakness it does have - the E-Ink on the other Kindle models is far easier on the eyes when doing heavy reading. I'm hanging on to my Kindle 3 for that reason. The kind of reading I'll be doing on my Fire is more along the lines of magazine reading, looking at recipes, newspaper articles, stuff like that.

Overall, the Fire is a solid purchase. If you're thinking about buying it, just do it. You won't be disappointed!
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

Munitio SV Mobile Performance Earphones with 3 Button Mic Control, Bronze Lower and mid end earphones have generally been lacking in both quality and performance. Given my propensity to misplace them, I have been reluctant to invest in more expensive versions. But with increased reliance on mobile devices, it was most definitely time to upgrade.

My familiarity with Munitio was more from their urban chic style complete with bullet motif, Kevlar coated cord, "tactical" carrying case and "hollow point" ear cups. At the risk of looking more Duck dynasty than cool, I was eager to try them.

Designed for use with Apple devices, the phones come securely packaged in a black carrying case. The look is sleek and modern and the bronze color is appealing. These are also available in black and gray. There are three sets of ear cups in different sizes. They were comfortable and shut out outside noise. The cord is flat and tangle free with a heft that promises durability. The 3 button mic control is located on the upper left hand side of the earphone cable. I really couldn't see the buttons but quickly mastered them by touch. They provide full functionality for calls and music on iPods, iPods and iPhones and just music for other mp3 players and Android devices.

I encountered no difficulties in making or taking calls. I could hear the other party and they could hear me without difficulty. The mic is positioned close enough to the mouth and is sufficiently sensitive that I didn't have to scream or repeat things. I made calls from a fairly busy coffee shop and a mall and ambient noise did not impair the call quality.

I tried these earphones with my IPod and a cheap mp3 player of dubious lineage. The sound was clear, strong and enjoyable. I did not find the bass overwhelming and was generally pleased with the performance.

Bottom line, I liked these earphones. The case and the trio of ear cups are thoughtful touches. Although light, there is a sense of substance and quality. The controls are intuitive and easy to use. There is a two year limited warranty. Serving up generous doses of comfort, convenience and performance, these ear phones are right on target.

Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor This little device does a lot.
While it is sort of a smart watch, it sort of isn't, too. But what it does, it does well.

The good:
- Excellent selection of watch faces, including cute, clever, big, pretty, etc. You can change your face every day to match your clothes if you want.
- If I understand correctly, you can use it with other services, like Spark People.
- measures pulse, steps, miles. Tracks exercise on demand.
- motivates in numerous ways. Reminders to stand up, encouragement to finish your goal steps for the hour, challenges, even "travel" challenges that are longer term.
- large userbase. You can network with more of your friends on Fitbit than on any other fitness watch.
- big face without losing attractiveness
- large variety of replacement bands available from third parties, some very pretty.
- Can be used with many other fitness applications.
- Detects sleep surprisingly accurately
- Lots of settings options
- A decent number of apps available
- Handles the shower well
- If you never have to take it off except to charge, it's harder to lose it.
- Charges very quickly
- The charger is an awesome design and easy to use
- You can always have your alarms with you so you never miss them.

The irritating
- All changes have to be made through the app.
- If you don't sync often enough, it loses your data
- Sync can take a long time.
- The battery life is considerably shorter than I expected. It's about 2 1/2 days if I have constant sync turned off.
- Don't even bother with constant sync unless you're willing to take it off to charge a lot.
- All the music apps are paid

All in all, though, the pros are big and the cons are small. Enough that it still warrants a 5 star review.

Western Digital 320GB WD Black Performance Mobile Hard Drive - 7200 RPM Class, SATA 6 Gb/s, , 32 MB Cache, 2.5" - WD3200LPLX Update 8-7-19: I went to the WD website to register my two drives. They show as no warranty from WD, presumably because they were bought through a reseller. Just so you know ...

I use these as primary storage (and backup storage) for our MacBook Air laptop. Most MacBooks now come with solid state drives, meaning memory chip based drives, not physical spinning disks. They are much more expensive than the heritage physical disk approach, such that the largest SSD that we could get with our 2017 MacBook Air was a 256 GB drive. These WD Black (virtually enterprise level) drives are 500 GB each, so our storage is 2x that of the built in drive. We use one as our primary external drive; once a month we install the 2nd drive (also externally), copy the files across, and put it into our safe deposit box at the bank. If we ever lose a drive, whether to failure or someone breaking in and stealing our drive and laptop, we're only 30 days behind, a real advantage.

The only downside to this drive is that the warranty on the drive itself is provided by the Seller, OEMGENUINE. The drive came marked with a label on the drive as a Seller 5 year warranty, with no terms provided. The downside risk is there is no published warranty, either by the Seller or by WD on their website, and whatever warranty is provided is subject to the Seller still being in existence over the next 5 years. However, given the price of the drive ($35 or so), it was a reasonable risk to take, especially since we acquired two and use one as the backup to the primary one. The odds of losing two drives at the same time is pretty remote. So we accepted the risk, but dropped the review for the product & seller by 1 star. If you go to the WD website, they do claim a 5 year limited warranty. I am a little surprised that the WD website doesn't provide a link to their warranty. So if we can't reach OEMGENUINE should we have a problem, I'm not sure what protection we'll have from WD. Something to consider if that's important to you.

These are fast drives (7200 rpm for the 500GB drive), which is noticeably faster than the previous bulk drives we've purchased online and/or removed from existing systems, which have all been 5400 rpm drives. SATA compatible, plug and play, no issues yet but it's only been a few days. If something materially changes, I'll post an update.
text_fidelity_b: Western Digital 320GB WD Black Performance Mobile Hard Drive - 7200 RPM Class, SATA 6 Gb/s, , 32 MB Cache, 2.5" - WD3200LPLX

HAOHUNT Camcorder Digital Video Camera HD 1080P 30fps 3.0 INCH Touch Screen 24MP Camcorder with Microphone and Wide Angle Lens Vlogging Camera with Remote Control Infrared Night Vision Recorder This digital camcorder has features not found on many camcorders.
First the things I like about this Camcorder:
This camcorder records in high definition (1020 at 30 fps), and two low resolution (720P at both 30 and 60 fps) select-able from the screen.
There is a option for setting the camera up for motion control triggered recording.
The system has a IR based night vision system to record in total blackout conditions.
The remote can be used to control most modes of the camcorder and start/stop recording.
This system comes with a external mic to help in recording the audio component of your filming, you have the option to use this mic or not depending on your circumstances.
You can use the camcorder as a photo camera with resolutions ranging from 5mp to 24mp along with settings for white balance, color, and shutter speeds.
You can turn off the beep sound for camera functions, something you may use if recording wildlife.
This Camcorder comes with a wide view lens, great when recording in a shallow area such as a room to get everyone and everything into one shot.
Extra battery, handy for extended use or areas where you cannot recharge the camera.

Things I would like to see improved:
The zoom is digital only, not an optical zoom. This limits the camcorder to recording only items in a shallow depth, not great for outdoor use unless you are up close to your subject.

All in all, a decent camcorder for use where you are close (physically) to your subject, or as long as you understand its limitations.
text_fidelity_b: HAOHUNT Camcorder Digital Video Camera HD 1080P 30fps 3.0 INCH Touch Screen 24MP Camcorder with Microphone and Wide Angle Lens Vlogging Camera with Remote Control Infrared Night Vision Recorder

text_fidelity_a:
Power Strip Individual Switch, 6 Outlets Metal Heavy Duty Surge Protector 6FT Cord 15A 120V 1800W for Home Office School Garden Industrial Aquarium (Black) I very much like that each outlet on this power strip has its own switch. It allows me to cut power to something that is plugged in without having to unplug anything. The switch lights up when it's powered so you can easily spot which outlets are active. It's a very handy design.

Unfortunately, the build quality is just average. The case is decent, and the power cord is nice and stout, but the rocker switches are pretty low-end. There's a lot of play in them, and while there is a positive click when it's depressed, it has a very cheap feel. The surge protection level is very basic. I'm fine with it since I'm using this to control pumps rather than electronics, but if you're looking for good quality surge protection, 300 Joules is not going to cut it at all.

While the presence of independent switches is a great addition, taking everything into consideration puts my rating at 3 stars (average) even when accounting for the price point. There are better made power strips with independent switches at around the same price, and the limited surge protection adds little to the overall value of this.
text_fidelity_b: Power Strip Individual Switch, 6 Outlets Metal Heavy Duty Surge Protector 6FT Cord 15A 120V 1800W for Home Office School Garden Industrial Aquarium (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlaySport (Zx3) HD Waterproof Pocket Video Camera (Purple) There's a lot to like about the Playsport. For one, it's very easy to use as a point and shoot should be. The picture quality is certainly fine for just about anybody's use, save for those who really like blowing their pictures up large. It's very fast to move between photos and movie--a few thumb moves is all it takes. The same for toggling between the movie quality. Which means if you suddenly want to grab a still photo while videoing or are worried about recording room and want to drop down a notch or two in quality, you can do so without missing a lot of action. The zoom is a 3X, which is serviceable. I'd prefer longer and I'm sure the next version will offer a longer zoom, but as I use this for quick shots of the family and not for event shooting, the 3X is rarely an issue in terms of not being adequate.

Transfer of files is easy and fast (I use a Mac) and all the cables come bundled with it. Yes, you read that right--it ships with all the needed cables.

Because it is so small and slim, and held in that vertical position, it can get a bit shaky and you'll need to pay attention to keeping it steady, more so than larger cameras or ones you hold with two hands horizontally. The sound pickup is fine save that wind noise can be a problem on windy days--it'll wash out a good deal of the speaking sound.

It feels rugged out of the box and the number of times I've dropped it, including just recently while chasing my boy and his friend around the corner of the house and getting my foot caught in the extension cord of the Halloween decorations. I watched the camera skid across several feet of concrete sidewalk but it was none the worse for wear.

It's slimness makes it a great pocket camera--one of those where it's defined as such not because you can cram it into your pocket and walk around like you have a grapefruit in there but where it slips right in and you barely notice it. That's one of the reasons it's become the camera I take most often when I know I won't need a larger zoom or a flash.

I haven't tried the underwater aspect in actual underwater conditions (snorkeling, say), but a few practice photos in the pool shows it takes pretty sharp photos in that environment. But I'll leave the gauging of that aspect to those more well-versed in such a need.

In the end, it's a great little camera and as mentioned, it's quickly become the one I carry along most often when we're just heading out for some family fun. For post-dusk indoor, I take a Canon elph and for events or hiking a Canon IS with a 12x zoom and a tele-converter. But for playing games in the yard, birthday parties, classroom events, etc.--the Kodak has become the go-to camera.

highly recommended
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlaySport (Zx3) HD Waterproof Pocket Video Camera (Purple)
